newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields continue to probe higher.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields continue to probe higher.

text.p: *Australian bond yields continued to probe higher as the market corrected the rally which took the long end below 7.0 percent earlier this week.
*Soft U.S. Treasuries add to the negative tone.

Australian bond yields continued to probe higher as the market corrected the rally which took the long end below 7.0 percent earlier this week, although turnover was light, suggesting the move was largely trader driven.
The tone at the shorter end of curve remained heavy as the market pushed back its expectations on the timing of a widely speculated easing by the Reserve Bank, traders said.
"There is disappointment the RBA hasn't cut rates, although the bill strip hasn't given up the chances of an easing completely," said one trader at a European based bank in Sydney.
September bill futures at around 94.80 are still indicating a cash rate well below current official 5.5 percent interest rates, but have recoiled from the 94.94 peak seen on Monday.
Analysts now believe that if the RBA is going to ease again it will be more likely to be around the time of the board meeting on July 1 and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2.

Last week's extremely weak labour force report, on top of the recent spate of soft data, fuelled expectations of an easing, but the subsequent fragility of the Australian dollar is being cited as one reason why the RBA may be holding back.
An easier close in U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday, which ended a three-day rally, added to the local negative tone.
The U.S. move came despite a benign U.S. CPI report for May, although the outcome was largely built in following a weak PPI last Friday.

There is still some uncertainty as to whether FOMC will tighten policy when it meets in July, which could have a bearing on local policy if it does, but the recent flow of data seems to suggest it will refrain this time round, analysts said.
Meanwhile, Westpac's leading index for April will be the last piece of local data for a over a week.
The market continued to correct against the dollar bloc after its strong outperformance which followed last week's labour force report.
